You make a map that answers a question about this codebase, for someone semi-technical. Explore with Read, Grep and Glob, then return the map as JSON. You cannot edit anything.

## The question
"Explain the map drafting loop between Claude and codemap: which steps are deterministic code and which are AI-driven?"

## What a good map is
- It follows what happens, in order, from where it starts (a button, a route, a job, a command) to where it ends (a table write, an email, an outside API), or to where it stops.
- 2–6 `areas` named in product language (Patients, Billing, Background jobs), not folder names.
- 4–12 boxes (`nodes`). Each is one step a person would recognize. `name`: plain English, at most 30 characters ("Patient marked enrolled", not "markConverted()").
- `kind`: entry (a way in), step, store (table, queue, cache), external (outside service), job (scheduled or background work).
- `explain` for every box: `concept` (1–2 plain sentences, no jargon), `how` (the mechanism; define any term you use), `code` (function and file names).
- Arrow `label`: 1–3 words saying how one step leads to the next ("sends request", "calls", "announces", "every night").
- When the trail stops, or something that should be connected isn't, record an `absence`: the `claim` in plain words, the two boxes it should connect (`between`), and the exact `search` that proves nothing is there (`pattern`, `regex`, optional `paths` globs), with `matches` set to the count that search returns (usually 0). Run that search yourself with Grep first.
- Code that exists but isn't reached from the start can still be boxes. Don't draw arrows that don't exist; use an absence.

## Evidence rules (a program checks every claim; anything it can't confirm is shown as unconfirmed)
- Every box and arrow cites at least one line: `file` (repo-relative), `line` (1-based), and `text` copied exactly from that line. A distinctive fragment of 10–80 characters works best.
- A box that is a function or method gets `symbol`: "<file>#<name>" (methods as Class.method, object members as obj.member, e.g. "src/db.ts#db.update").
- Arrow `kind`: `calls` when a function in the from box literally calls the function in the to box; `request` when an HTTP call in the from box hits a route handled by the to box; `imports`; `then` for anything else (events, ordering). The checker verifies calls, request and imports against the code, so use them only when literally true.
- Never cite or read secret files (.env, keys).

## Walkthrough (`tour`, written last)
- 4–7 stops in the order a newcomer should read them: what the map shows → the path → the problem, if there is one → what it means.
- Each stop: `title`, `text` (2–3 plain sentences), `focus` (ids of the areas, nodes, edges or absences it's about), optional `terms` it uses that need defining, and `ask` with 1–2 good next questions.
- Point stops only at boxes, arrows and absences you're confident in.

1	// Making a map: a head start from the code facts, Claude explores and drafts, the checker re-reads the code, and Claude
2	// gets up to `repairs` chances to fix what didn't check out. The best attempt wins; nothing unconfirmed is hidden.
3	import { check, parseMap, type CheckReport, type CodeMap } from '@codemap/core';
4	import type { Agent, Progress } from './agent';
5	import { headStart } from './hints';
6	import { evidenceRepairPrompt, makerPrompt, shapeRepairPrompt } from './prompts';
7	import { MAP_SCHEMA } from './schemas';
8	
9	export type Status = { kind: 'status'; text: string };
10	export type MakeOptions = {
11	  root: string;
12	  question: string;
13	  agent: Agent;
14	  model?: string;
15	  repairs?: number;
16	  onProgress?: (p: Progress | Status) => void;
17	  signal?: AbortSignal;
18	};
19	export type MakeResult = { map: CodeMap; report: CheckReport; sessionId: string | null; cost: number; rounds: number };
20	
21	const withQuestion = (output: unknown, question: string) =>
22	  output && typeof output === 'object' ? { ...(output as Record<string, unknown>), version: 1, question } : output;
23	
24	export async function makeMap(o: MakeOptions): Promise<MakeResult> {
25	  const status = (text: string) => o.onProgress?.({ kind: 'status', text });
26	  status('Scanning the code for ways in, routes and tables');
27	  const hints = await headStart(o.root);
28	  status('Claude is exploring the code');
29	  const run = (prompt: string, resume: string | null) =>
30	    o.agent({ prompt, schema: MAP_SCHEMA, cwd: o.root, resume, model: o.model, onProgress: o.onProgress, signal: o.signal });
31	
32	  let res = await run(makerPrompt(o.question, hints.text), null);
33	  let cost = res.cost ?? 0;
34	  let rounds = 1;
35	  let best: { map: CodeMap; report: CheckReport } | null = null;
36	  let lastProblems: string[] = [];
37	
38	  for (let attempt = 0; ; attempt++) {
39	    const parsed = parseMap(withQuestion(res.output, o.question));
40	    let repair: string | null = null;
41	    if (!parsed.ok) {
42	      lastProblems = parsed.problems;
43	      repair = shapeRepairPrompt(parsed.problems);
44	    } else {
45	      status('Checking every claim against the code');
46	      const report = check(parsed.map, o.root);
47	      if (!best || report.summary.unconfirmed < best.report.summary.unconfirmed) best = { map: parsed.map, report };
48	      status(`${report.summary.confirmed} of ${report.summary.claims} claims confirmed`);
49	      if (report.summary.unconfirmed > 0) repair = evidenceRepairPrompt(report);
50	    }
51	    if (!repair || attempt >= (o.repairs ?? 2)) break;
52	    status(parsed.ok ? 'Asking Claude to fix the claims that didn\'t check out' : 'Asking Claude to fix the map\'s structure');
53	    res = await run(repair, res.sessionId);
54	    cost += res.cost ?? 0;
55	    rounds++;
56	  }
57	  if (!best) throw new Error(`Claude's map couldn't be read: ${lastProblems.slice(0, 5).join('; ')}`);
58	  return { ...best, sessionId: res.sessionId, cost, rounds };
59	}

3	description: Draw a checked, interactive map that answers how something in this codebase works ("what happens when a user signs up?", "where does this email get sent?", "how does billing connect to accounts?"). Use when the user wants to understand a flow, asks how parts connect, or asks for a map, diagram or walkthrough of the code. Every box and arrow on the map is verified against the code.
4	---
5	
6	# codemap
7	
8	codemap turns a question about this repo into a map the person can explore in their browser: areas of the app, the
9	steps in order, labeled arrows, and red dashed arrows where something that should be connected isn't. A plain program
10	checks every claim against the code before it's shown. In the map they can take a walkthrough, select any box or arrow
11	and ask about it, and approve fixes that codemap applies and re-checks.
12	
13	## When to use it
14	
15	- The user asks how something works across several files: "what happens when…", "how does X reach Y", "where does Z
16	  get triggered".
17	- The user is about to change code they don't understand yet and wants to see it first.
18	- The user asks for a map, diagram, graph or walkthrough of part of the code.
19	
20	Don't use it for a question about a single line or function; answer that directly.
21	
22	## How to run it
23	
24	Run from the repo root (or pass `--repo`). Use the user's question in their own words:
25	
26	```bash
27	codemap "What happens when a patient converts?" --repo "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
28	```
29	
30	It starts a small local server, explores the code with Claude (about a minute for a small repo), and prints a link
31	like `http://127.0.0.1:4317/m/<id>?t=<token>`. Give the user that link and tell them to open it. The command keeps
32	running to serve the map: run it in the background, and don't wait for it to exit.
33	
34	Other commands:
35	
36	- `codemap open` lists the maps already made in this repo (they're saved under `.codemap/maps/`).
37	- `codemap check <map-id>` re-checks a saved map against the current code and prints anything that no longer holds.
38	  It exits with 1 if a claim fails, so it can run in CI.
39	
40	## Notes
41	
42	- codemap reads the code and never changes it, except for a fix the user approves in the map.
43	- It never reads secret files (`.env`, keys) and only listens on 127.0.0.1.
44	- It needs Claude access: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or a logged-in Claude Code.
45	- If `codemap` isn't on the PATH, it hasn't been installed. Tell the user to install it from the codemap repo
46	  (see its README) instead of guessing another command.
47

6	const MAX_LINES = 40;
7	const section = (title: string, lines: string[]) =>
8	  lines.length ? [`${title}:`, ...lines.slice(0, MAX_LINES), ...(lines.length > MAX_LINES ? [`  …and ${lines.length - MAX_LINES} more`] : []), ''] : [];
9	
10	export async function headStart(root: string): Promise<{ text: string; scan: RepoScan | null }> {
11	  await initTreeSitter();
12	  let scan: RepoScan;

21	  const routes = facts.flatMap((f) => f.routes);
22	  const routeLines = routes.map((r) => `  - ${r.method} ${r.path} → ${r.handler ?? r.file}`);
23	
24	  const fetchFiles = facts
25	    .filter((f) => /\.(tsx?|jsx?|mjs|cjs)$/.test(f.path))
26	    .flatMap((f) => {
27	      const source = fs.readFileSync(`${root}/${f.path}`, 'utf8');
28	      return /\bfetch\(|axios|ky\./.test(source) ? [{ path: f.path, source, symbols: f.symbols }] : [];
29	    });

31	    const m = matchRoute(site, routes);

33	  });

36	  for (const f of facts) for (const w of f.writes) writers.set(w.table, (writers.get(w.table) ?? new Set()).add(w.symbol ?? f.path));
37	  const tables = [...writers].map(([t, by]) => `  - ${t} ← ${[...by].slice(0, 4).join(', ')}`);
38
